Molten Ventures
Results analysis from Kepler Trust Intelligence

Molten Ventures (GROW) has reported strong results for the half year ending 30/09/2026, with the NAV per share up 15%, continuing the momentum seen over the past two years. The gross portfolio net fair value movement was positive 16%.

The most important drivers of return were the two largest positions, ICEYE and Revolut, both of which saw significant fair value uplifts. Molten realised £93m from these two investments over the period, out of total realisations of £109m. These were achieved at a multiple on invested capital (MOIC) of 14.1x for ICEYE and 19x for Revolut. A further £50m was realised from Revolut post period end, at an even higher MOIC.

Much of this cash has been reinvested into less mature investments, such as Isar Aerospace. Post period end, Isar became the first commercial space company from Europe to successfully deliver satellites into orbit, and the company has yet to be valued since the news.

Another important milestone was first close of the Molten Ventures Growth Fund, with £175m raised including a £75m cornerstone commitment from the British Business Bank. This highlights the strong policy support for the venture space, particularly in the strategic tech that Molten often targets.
Kepler view

To us, these results say very much that Molten Ventures (GROW) is back – any post-2022 lull seems well and truly over, with the portfolio motoring along as intended. Molten’s gross portfolio net fair value movement of 16% for the reporting period, or 32% annualised, is above the long run target of 20%, while realisations of 10% are in line with target. The high conviction positions within the portfolio continue to drive returns and provide realisation opportunities, generating lots of cash to reinvest in new ideas. Critically, this is not a Molten-only story – activity in the European VC space looks healthy, with 2026 on course to deliver the highest deal value since 2022 if the pace is maintained, according to PitchBook. Additionally, capital raised has nearly broken through 2025’s total amount, which would reverse a multi-year trend of decline.

In part this reflects the impact of the EU’s Scale up Europe fund, which aims to back the world class science and technology pioneered in Europe and allow the businesses to mature and scale. The UK has also launched initiatives with similar ends, Molten winning a cornerstone investment from the British Business Bank for its Molten Ventures Growth fund. There is clear political awareness of the strategic importance of emerging tech for European countries in a world of rising geopolitical tensions and rapidly emerging new technologies, as well as its economic potential. The success of ICEYE has been fostered by significant contract wins for European armed forces, as they recognise the importance of satellite delivery for strategic defence in space. Similarly, Isar Aerospace’s potential to be a European SpaceX is important if Europe is to improve its strategic independence from the US, particularly in the light of reports that SpaceX will stop taking commercial Falcon 9 launch bookings beyond 2028.

We think Molten offers a unique opportunity to invest in a flourishing European tech sector at the early stage, with a diverse portfolio of unlisted businesses that can’t be accessed elsewhere. These results show a number of companies are making strong progress at the stock level, while the VC space is enjoying some powerful tailwinds, and they underline the attractions of the industry at a time when multiple new technologies are creating exciting potential.
